chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar said: He narrated to me Abu Sa'id Sahl ibn Zyad al-Adamy, who said: He narrated to us al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, from Ali ibn Hafs al-Abasi, from al-Salt ibn al-Ala', from Abu al-Hazoor, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
The people were created from various trees, but I and the son of Abu Talib were created from one tree; I am its trunk and Ja'far is its branch.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual origin of the Prophet and Ali ibn Abi Talib according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* articulates the Shia doctrine of *Al-Wilayah* and spiritual unity, positing that the Prophet and Imam Ali share a singular, primordial essence distinct from the rest of humanity. The metaphor of the 'single tree' underscores their inseparable spiritual authority, with the mention of Ja'far likely referring to Ja'far al-Sadiq to extend this lineage of purity through the Imams. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the Ahl al-Bayt not merely as family, but as the unique source of divine guidance.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-72 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted on the authority of Abu Sa’id Sahl ibn Zyad al-Adamy, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn al-Hussein al-Lu’lu’ee, on the authority of Ali ibn Hafs al-Abasi, on the authority of Al-Salt ibn al-Ala’, on the authority of Abil-Hozoor, on the authority of Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “
The people were created from several roots. Ibn Abi Talib and I were created from the same root. Ali is my trunk, and Ja’far is my branch.”
